q-81394.name: Question 1
q-81394.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}-{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{2} & =5{c}_{3}+2{c}_{2}, \\ {b}_{3} & ={c}_{2}-{c}_{1},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ a & b & 1 \\ -1 & c & 0\end{aligned}]?
$$
q-81394.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $c=5.$

q-81394.html:
Question 1
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2,c3} be bases of R3. What are the values of a,b, and c if

b1=c1+2c2−c3,b2=5c3+2c2,b3=c2−c1,

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is

PB→C=[10−1ab1−1c0]?

a
a=2, b=0, and c=−1
b
a=1, b=−2, and c=5
c
a=0, b=2, and c=−1
d
a=1, b=2, and c=0
e
a=2, b=2, and c=5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The coordinates of the vectors in B relative to the basis C are

[b1]C=[12−1],[b2]C=[025],[b3]C=[−110].

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of B relative to the basis C.

Therefore, we obtain

PB→C=[10−1221−150].

Finally, a=2, b=2, and c=5.

q-113104.name: Question 2
q-113104.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ 
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ from $B$ to $C$ given that

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-113104.worked_solution:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-113104.html:
Question 2
?

Let B={b1,b2} and C={c1,c2} be bases of R2. Find the change-of-coordinates matrix PB→C from B to C given that

[b1]C=[5−2],[b2]C=[5−1].

a
[−15−25]
b
[55−2−1]
c
[5−1−25]
d
[5−25−1]
e
[−255−1]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of B relative to the basis C.

Therefore, we obtain

PB→C=[55−2−1].

q-81825.name: Question 3
q-81825.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} & =3{b}_{3}-{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}, \\ {c}_{2} & =4{b}_{2}-5{b}_{1}, \\ {c}_{3} & =2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}a & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & b & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & c\end{aligned}]?
$$
q-81825.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $C$ relative to the basis $B$ are

$$
[{c}_{1}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[{c}_{2}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[{c}_{3}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=-1,$ $b=4,$ and $c=3.$

a

c
a=−1, b=4, and c=3

Correct
EXPLANATION

The coordinates of the vectors in C relative to the basis B are

[c1]B=[−113],[c2]B=[−540],[c3]B=[203].

Therefore, we obtain

PC→B=[−1−52140303].

Finally, a=−1, b=4, and c=3.

q-113105.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ If ${b}_{1}=2{c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}={c}_{1}-2{c}_{2},$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ from $B$ to $C.$
q-113105.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-36354.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ be bases of ${R}^{3}.$ 
What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & =2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{2} & =4{c}_{1}-2{c}_{3}, \\ {b}_{3} & =2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and  the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & a & 2 \\ b & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & c & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
q-36354.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C$ are

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=4,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=-2.$

q-36354.html:
Question 5
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} and C={c1,c2,c3} be bases of R3. What are the values of a,b, and c if

b1=2c1−c2+c3,b2=4c1−2c3,b3=2c1−3c3,

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is

PB→C=[2a2b001c−3]?

a
a=1, b=4, and c=0
b
a=4, b=−1, and c=−2
c
a=4, b=1, and c=2
d
a=2, b=0, and c=4
e
a=−1, b=4, and c=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The coordinates of the vectors in B relative to the basis C are

[b1]C=[2−11],[b2]C=[40−2],[b3]C=[20−3].

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of B relative to the basis C.

Therefore, we obtain

PB→C=[242−1001−2−3].

Finally, a=4, b=−1, and c=−2.

q-36402.name: Question 6
q-36402.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{2}.$ 
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to S}$ from $B$ to $S$ if 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$
q-36402.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ consists of the vectors ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2},$ given by

$$
{e}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The components of the vectors of $B$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\,\text{ and }\,[{b}_{2}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $S.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -6 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and let S be the standard basis of R2. Find the change-of-coordinates matrix PB→S from B to S if b1=[1−6],b2=[−19].

a
[1−1−69]
b
[−6−911]
c
[−9161]
d
[−611−9]
e
[1−1−96]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that the standard basis of R2 consists of the vectors e1 and e2, given by e1=[10],e2=[01].

The components of the vectors of B are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

[b1]S=[1−6] and [b2]S=[−19].

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to S is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of B relative to the basis S.

Therefore, we obtain PB→S=[1−1−69].

q-113342.name: Question 7
q-113342.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{2}.$ 
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to S}$ from $B$ to $S$ if 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
q-113342.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ consists of the vectors ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2},$ given by

$$
{e}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The components of the vectors of $B$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $S.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-36366.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{2}.$ 
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to S}$ from $B$ to $S$ if 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
q-36366.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ consists of the vectors ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2},$ given by

$$
{e}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The components of the vectors of $B$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $S.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

q-81852.name: Question 9
q-81852.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -9\end{aligned}],
$$

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is 

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}3 & a & 7 \\ -1 & 4 & b \\ 4 & c & -9\end{aligned}].
$$
q-81852.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ consists of the vectors ${e}_{1},{e}_{2},$ and ${e}_{3},$ given by

$$
{e}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The components of the vectors in $B$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -9\end{aligned}]
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $S.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 7 \\ -1 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 7 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=8,$ $b=5,$ and $c=7.$

Question 9
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and let S be the standard basis of R3. What are the values of a,b, and c if

b1=[3−14],b2=[847],b3=[75−9],

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from B to S is

PB→S=[3a7−14b4c−9].

a
a=8, b=5, and c=7.
b
a=7, b=5, and c=8.
c
a=8, b=−1, and c=7.
d
a=−1, b=7, and c=5.
e
a=−1, b=8, and c=5.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the standard basis of R3 consists of the vectors e1,e2, and e3, given by e1=[100],e2=[010],e3=[001].

The components of the vectors in B are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

[b1]S=[3−14],[b2]S=[847],[b3]S=[75−9]

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to S is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of B relative to the basis S.

Therefore, we obtain PB→S=[387−14547−9].

Finally, a=8, b=5, and c=7.

q-81850.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],
$$

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is 

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & a \\ b & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & c & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
q-81850.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ consists of the vectors ${e}_{1},{e}_{2},$ and ${e}_{3},$ given by

$$
{e}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The components of the vectors in $B$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

$$
[{b}_{1}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{2}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[{b}_{3}]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $S.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3 \\ 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=0,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=-5.$
